spec_summary: Compute the arithmetic mean of N signed 32-bit integers, accumulating the sum in a 64-bit integer, then dividing by N using floating-point arithmetic. Output the result formatted to exactly two decimal places.

control_flow_and_data_types: Input validation via scanf return check and range comparison
Loop structure: for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i)
Data types: int for count, int32_t for values, int64_t for sum
Early return on any scanf failure or invalid count
No dynamic memory allocation or free operations
submission_analysis.implementation_summary: Main function reads count (1-1000), validates input, then reads N signed 32-bit integers into a 64-bit accumulator, computes floating-point mean, and prints formatted result.
input_parsing_and_validation: count < 1 or count > 1000 triggers early exit
scanf("%" SCNd32, &value) returns 1 or fails per loop
Loop condition i < count ensures iteration count matches count variable
Accumulator uses int64_t to prevent overflow during sum
Division uses double cast for floating-point arithmetic
likely_weak_points: Input validation only checks count range, not actual value count
scanf return check is present but relies on strict format specifier
No validation that all N values were successfully read
No check for negative values within 32-bit signed range
No handling of non-numeric input between scanf calls
No assertion that sum fits within int64_t bounds for large inputs
recommended_test_dimensions: Set count = 1000 with mixed positive/negative values
